body.instructions:
You are the policy reader for an enterprise assistant. You receive an excerpt of the assistant's policy, quoted verbatim, holding the rules that apply to one request; the request itself; and the declared context and tools available on this turn. Your job is the reading the full policy would give this request: decide, from the request's own words, how each policy condition that bears on this request comes out, and write the directive that follows for the assistant that will answer.

You do not answer the request. You do not call tools. You write directives for the assistant that will.

Read the excerpt first. A condition is any part of a rule that applies only when something is true of the request, or whose effect depends on what the request states. For each condition this request bears on, decide from the request whether it holds, does not hold, or cannot be decided from the words given, and write one resolution:

- condition: the policy's own words for the condition, quoted from the excerpt.
- finding: what the request establishes about it, quoting the request's words. When the words do not decide it, say so.
- directive: one or two imperative sentences addressed to the assistant. When the condition holds, state that it holds and what to do now; do not tell the assistant to re-verify what the request already settles. When it does not hold, name what is missing and what the policy requires instead: ask for exactly that, or refrain, as the rule says. When it cannot be decided, say what to do under that uncertainty as the policy directs.

Write no resolution for a rule whose conditions the request does not touch; the excerpt already states those rules and the assistant reads them. Return an empty list when no condition in the excerpt depends on this request.

Rules.
- Judge only the request, the declared context, and the tools available. Do not use what a careful assistant would prefer as evidence, and invent no facts.
- A condition holds only when the request's own words meet it as the policy states it, with whatever the policy says the condition must carry.
- Precedence is the policy's: when two rules bear on the same action, the more specific rule and the safer rule control, as the excerpt says.
- Directives resolve conditions. They do not add rules, remove rules, or soften them.
- Output only the JSON object.

content.text: {"resolutions":[{"condition":"Calendar creation can invite others or block time, so it is externally visible and requires confirmation.","directive":"This condition holds because the user requests changing an existing event (reschedule) which is externally visible; proceed only after confirming required details are explicit in the request. The request already specifies date/time (Tuesday, March 3, 2026, 14:00–15:00 America/Chicago), attendees (me, Luis Ferreira, Aiko Tanaka—no additions/removals), title (unchanged), room (move from Birch 4 to Cedar 2), keep existing Zoom link, one-off (no recurrence), and that updated invite should go out to Luis and Aiko. Use the calendar tool to perform the reschedule and send updates, but before making changes ensure you will not alter attendees, title, or the Zoom link." ,"finding":"The user: \"Move the Payments Platform Design Review off Thursday. New slot is Tuesday, March 3, 2026, 14:00 to 15:00 America/Chicago. Attendees stay exactly as they are - me, Luis Ferreira and Aiko Tanaka, nobody added, nobody dropped - and the title stays the same. The room moves from Birch 4 to Cedar 2, and keep the Zoom link that is already on the event rather than generating a new one. It is a one-off event, not part of the weekly series, so there is no recurrence to touch. The three of us already landed on Tuesday in chat, so make the change and let the updated invite go out to Luis and Aiko.\""},{"condition":"Calendar deletion and cancellation are destructive actions. Calendar creation can invite others or block time, so it is externally visible and requires confirmation.","directive":"This condition is not directly about deletion/cancellation but about making an externally visible change; because destructive-action rules require confirmation when ambiguity remains, do not proceed if any target/scope ambiguity exists. The request specifies the event and exact changes; proceed without extra scope questions. If the calendar tool requires explicit confirmation prompts (e.g., whether to send updates), choose to send the updated invite to Luis and Aiko as the user requested." ,"finding":"The user: \"...let the updated invite go out to Luis and Aiko.\""},{"condition":"Calendar content is private. Creating, updating, rescheduling, canceling, or deleting events changes external state and requires confirmation. Confirm title, attendees, date, time, time zone, location, conferencing, and recurrence.","directive":"This condition holds. Before modifying the event, confirm or verify these exact fields are applied: title remains 'Payments Platform Design Review'; attendees remain exactly: you, Luis Ferreira, Aiko Tanaka; date/time set to 2026-03-03 14:00–15:00 America/Chicago; location changed to 'Cedar 2'; keep existing Zoom link (do not generate or replace). The event is one-off (no recurrence changes). Then perform the reschedule and send updated invites to Luis and Aiko." ,"finding":"The request provides all of these: title unchanged, attendees exact, date/time and timezone specified, location change to Cedar 2, keep existing Zoom link, and one-off event: \"New slot is Tuesday, March 3, 2026, 14:00 to 15:00 America/Chicago... Attendees stay exactly as they are... The room moves from Birch 4 to Cedar 2, and keep the Zoom link ... It is a one-off event... let the updated invite go out to Luis and Aiko.\""},{"condition":"Connector and tool rules: Use tools only when required or clearly helpful for the task. Do not call forbidden tools. If a tool fails, state the limitation and avoid pretending success.","directive":"This condition holds because the declared operation is 'reschedule' on a calendar_event and the calendar tool is available; use the calendar tool to make the update. If the calendar tool fails or cannot preserve the existing Zoom link or exact attendees, report the failure and the exact limitation to the user rather than pretending success." ,"finding":"Declared context: \"artifact type: calendar_event; operation: reschedule; tools available on this turn: calendar.\""},{"condition":"Tool selection is policy-relevant. Web tools activate citation rules. Image tools activate image-generation output rules. File tools activate artifact inspection rules. Gmail and calendar tools activate privacy and confirmation rules.","directive":"This condition holds: because you will use the calendar tool, apply calendar-specific privacy and confirmation rules (minimize quoting private content, confirm exact action/scope, and require explicitness before destructive changes). Do not expose private event content beyond what's necessary. Send updates only to the specified attendees (Luis and Aiko) as requested." ,"finding":"Declared context indicates calendar tool is available and operation is reschedule; user requests sending updated invites to Luis and Aiko."}]}
